question: What is the most important reason for doing a vehicle inspection?
choice_a: Safety for yourself and other road users
choice_b: To avoid paying a mechanic
choice_d: To satisfy the motor carrier's paperwork requirements
explanation: The manual states that safety is the most important reason to inspect your vehicle, for yourself and for other road users.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.1 Why Inspect

question: What is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on the front tires of a commercial vehicle?
choice_b: 1/32 inch
choice_d: 6/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.3 What to Look For, Tire Problems

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on tires other than the front tires?
choice_b: 2/32 inch
choice_d: 1/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires at least 2/32-inch tread depth on tires other than the front tires.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.3 What to Look For, Tire Problems

question: According to the manual, what is prohibited on the front wheels of a bus?
choice_b: Steel-belted tires
choice_d: Re-grooved, recapped, or retreaded tires
explanation: The manual states that re-grooved, recapped, or retreaded tires on the front wheels of a bus are prohibited.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.3 What to Look For, Tire Problems

question: A leaf spring missing or broken in what fraction of its leaves will put a vehicle "out of service"?
choice_b: All of the leaves
choice_d: One-fourth or more
explanation: The manual states that if one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring, it will put the vehicle out of service.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.3 What to Look For, Suspension System Defects

question: On a vehicle with a 20-inch steering wheel, what amount of play at the rim can indicate a dangerous steering defect?
choice_a: More than 45 degrees, about 6 inches of movement
choice_b: Any play at all, since play is never normal
choice_d: More than 10 degrees, about 2 inches of movement
explanation: The manual states that steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees (approximately 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel) can make it hard to steer.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.3 What to Look For, Steering System Defects

question: Besides a fire extinguisher and spare electrical fuses, what warning devices must a commercial vehicle carry?
choice_b: Three reflective triangles, or at least 6 fuses, or 3 liquid-burning flares
choice_d: A single reflective safety vest
explanation: The manual lists warning devices for parked vehicles as three reflective triangles or at least 6 fuses or 3 liquid-burning flares.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.3 What to Look For, Emergency Equipment

question: How long should a driver keep a copy of the vehicle inspection report in the vehicle?
choice_b: One month
choice_d: One week
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to keep a copy of the report in the vehicle for one day so the next driver can learn about any problems found.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.1 Test Your Knowledge

question: When approaching a vehicle to begin an inspection, what should a driver check for underneath it?
choice_b: Proper mud flap color
choice_c: Fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks
choice_d: Tire pressure readings
explanation: The manual directs drivers approaching the vehicle to look under it for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Approaching the Vehicle

question: Before raising the hood or tilting the cab to check the engine compartment, what should a driver first confirm?
choice_b: That the parking brakes are on and/or wheels are chocked
choice_c: That the mirrors are folded in
choice_d: That the fuel tank is full
explanation: Step 2 of the seven-step inspection method requires checking that the parking brakes are on and/or wheels are chocked before opening the engine compartment.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Step 2

question: When starting the engine, air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within what time frame?
choice_b: 1 minute
choice_d: 10 minutes
explanation: The manual states air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Step 3, Look at the Gauges

question: The governor cut-out pressure for an air brake system is usually in which range?
explanation: The manual states air pressure should build to the governor cut-out, usually around 120 to 140 psi.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Step 3, Look at the Gauges

question: When you start the engine, what should the ABS indicator light on the dash do if the system is working properly?
choice_b: Stay on continuously the whole trip
choice_d: Come on and then turn off
explanation: The manual states the ABS indicator light should come on and then turn off; if it stays on, the ABS is not working properly.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Step 3

question: On a trailer equipped with ABS, what indicates that the trailer's ABS is not working properly?
choice_a: The trailer brakes lock immediately when applied
choice_b: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on
choice_c: The parking brake will not release
choice_d: A buzzer sounds continuously in the cab
explanation: For trailers, if the yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on, the ABS is not working properly.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Step 3

question: During the walk-around inspection, how should a driver check lug nuts that show rust streaks?
choice_b: Ignore them since rust is only cosmetic
choice_c: Use a wrench to test for looseness
choice_d: Spray them with lubricant and move on
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to use a wrench to test rust-streaked lug nuts, which indicate possible looseness.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Step 5, Left Front Side

question: Drivers of trucks and truck tractors transporting cargo must inspect the cargo's securement within the first how many miles of a trip?
choice_b: 50 miles
choice_d: 10 miles
explanation: The manual requires an initial cargo securement inspection within the first 50 miles of a trip.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.6 Inspection during a Trip, Safety Inspection

question: After the initial 50-mile check, how often must cargo securement be rechecked during a trip?
choice_a: Every 50 miles or every hour, whichever comes first
choice_b: Every 500 miles or every eight hours
choice_c: Every 150 miles or every three hours, whichever comes first
choice_d: Only at the end of the trip
explanation: The manual requires cargo securement to be rechecked every 150 miles or every three hours, whichever comes first.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.6 Inspection during a Trip, Safety Inspection

question: To test a hydraulic brake system for leaks, a driver should pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold it for how long?
choice_b: 1 second
choice_d: 5 seconds
explanation: The manual states to pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold for five seconds; the pedal should not move.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.1.5 Seven-step Inspection Method, Step 7, Test for Hydraulic Leaks

question: When testing the parking brake during a vehicle inspection, what should a driver do after setting it and placing the vehicle in a low gear?
choice_a: Gently pull forward against the parking brake to make sure it holds
choice_b: Rev the engine to full throttle
choice_d: Turn off the engine and exit the cab
explanation: The manual describes gently pulling forward against the parking brake to make sure it holds as part of the brake system test.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Brake System, Test Parking Brake(s)

question: When testing service brake stopping action, about how fast should the vehicle be moving before firmly pushing the brake pedal?
choice_b: About 60 mph
choice_d: About 45 mph
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to go about five miles per hour, then push the brake pedal firmly to check for pulling or unusual pedal feel.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Brake System, Test Service Brake Stopping Action

question: To avoid rolling back when starting on an upgrade with a manual transmission, what should a driver do?
choice_a: Partly engage the clutch before taking the right foot off the brake
choice_b: Rely solely on the trailer's electrical brakes
choice_c: Shift immediately into the highest gear
choice_d: Release the clutch fully before applying any power
explanation: The manual advises partly engaging the clutch before taking your right foot off the brake, and using the parking brake as needed to keep from rolling back.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.2.1 Accelerating

question: If the drive wheels begin to spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, what should the driver do?
choice_b: Take the foot off the accelerator
choice_c: Press the accelerator harder to power through
choice_d: Shift into a higher gear right away
explanation: The manual states that if the drive wheels begin to spin, take your foot off the accelerator.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.2.1 Accelerating

question: How should a driver hold the steering wheel for safe control?
choice_a: With fingertips only for a quick release
choice_b: With both hands at the bottom of the wheel
choice_c: Firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
choice_d: With one hand loosely at the top
explanation: The manual instructs holding the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides so it does not pull away from your hands if you hit a curb or pothole.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.2.2 Steering

question: Because a driver cannot see everything behind a commercial vehicle, what general practice does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Avoid backing whenever possible, and park so you can pull forward when leaving
choice_b: Back at normal driving speed to minimize exposure time
choice_d: Always use a spotter connected by radio
explanation: The manual states that backing is always dangerous, so drivers should avoid backing whenever they can and try to park so they can pull forward when leaving.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.2.4 Backing Safely

question: Why does the manual recommend backing and turning toward the driver's side whenever possible?
choice_a: It allows the driver to see better by looking out the side window
choice_b: It is required by federal law in all states
choice_c: It reduces wear on the tires
choice_d: It is faster than backing to the right
explanation: Backing toward the driver's side lets the driver watch the rear of the vehicle by looking out the side window, whereas backing to the right is very dangerous because visibility is worse.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.2.4 Backing Safely, Back and Turn Toward the Driver's Side

question: Before backing with a helper, what should the driver and helper agree on?
choice_a: A specific speed limit for backing
choice_b: A set of hand signals, including a signal for "stop"
choice_d: Which mirror the helper should watch
explanation: The manual advises working out a set of hand signals before backing, and agreeing on a signal for "stop."
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.2.4 Backing Safely, Use a Helper

question: Double clutching to change gears is generally required for which type of transmission?
choice_b: Automatic transmissions
choice_d: All transmissions equally
explanation: The manual states that most heavy vehicles with unsynchronized manual transmissions require double clutching; if equipped with a synchronized manual transmission, double clutching is NOT required.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.3.1 Manual Transmissions

question: What are the two main ways a driver can know when to shift gears?
choice_b: Fuel level and oil pressure
choice_d: Engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph)
explanation: The manual describes using engine speed (rpm) via the tachometer or road speed (mph) via the speedometer to know when to shift.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.3.1 Manual Transmissions, Knowing When to Shift Up

question: Before starting down a hill, a driver should downshift to a gear that is usually what, compared to the gear needed to climb the same hill?
choice_b: A higher gear
choice_d: A lower gear
explanation: The manual states you should be in a low enough gear before starting down a hill, usually lower than the gear required to climb the same hill.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.3.1 Manual Transmissions, Before Starting Down a Hill

question: Why does the manual recommend downshifting to the right gear before entering a curve?
choice_b: To reduce engine noise
choice_c: It is only needed on wet roads
choice_d: To allow some power through the curve for stability and to speed up once out of the curve
explanation: The manual explains that downshifting before a curve lets you use some power through the curve to help the vehicle be more stable, and allows you to speed up as soon as you're out of the curve.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.3.1 Manual Transmissions, Before Entering a Curve

question: What is the purpose of a vehicle retarder?
choice_b: To help slow the vehicle and reduce brake wear
choice_d: To increase acceleration on hills
explanation: The manual states retarders help slow a vehicle, reducing the need for brakes and brake wear, and give another way to slow down.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.3.4 Retarders

question: Why should a driver turn off the retarder when the road is wet, icy, or snow-covered?
choice_a: The retarder may cause the drive wheels to skid due to poor traction
choice_b: Retarders are illegal on all public roads
choice_c: Retarders drain the battery in cold weather
choice_d: It has no effect on the vehicle either way
explanation: The manual warns that when drive wheels have poor traction, the retarder may cause them to skid, so it should be turned off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.3.4 Retarders, Caution

question: On a vehicle with an automatic transmission, what does selecting a low range help achieve when going down a grade?
choice_b: Automatic activation of the retarder
choice_c: Reduced fuel consumption at highway speed
choice_d: Faster acceleration
explanation: The manual states a low range gives greater engine braking when going down grades, and it is important to use this braking effect.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.3.3 Automatic Transmissions

question: About how many seconds ahead do most good drivers look while driving?
choice_b: 2 to 4 seconds
choice_d: 5 to 8 seconds
explanation: The manual states that most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.4.1 Seeing Ahead

question: At highway speeds, looking 12 to 15 seconds ahead corresponds to about what distance?
choice_b: A quarter of a mile
choice_d: One block
explanation: The manual states that at highway speeds, looking 12 to 15 seconds ahead is about a quarter of a mile (at lower speeds it's about one block).
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.4.1 Seeing Ahead, How Far Ahead to Look

question: When should mirror adjustment be checked for accuracy?
choice_b: Once a year during scheduled maintenance
choice_c: Only when a passenger points out a problem
choice_d: Before the start of any trip, when the trailer(s) are straight
explanation: The manual states mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.4.2 Seeing to the Sides and Rear, Mirror Adjustment

question: Which of the following does the manual identify as a special situation requiring more frequent mirror checks?
choice_b: Idling at a red light
choice_c: Driving on a straight, empty rural highway
choice_d: Lane changes, turns, merges, and tight maneuvers
explanation: The manual lists lane changes, turns, merges, and tight maneuvers as special situations that require more than regular mirror checks.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.4.2 Seeing to the Sides and Rear, Special Situations

question: What is true about how objects appear in a convex ("fisheye") mirror?
choice_a: They appear at their exact true size and distance
choice_b: They appear larger and closer than they really are
choice_d: They appear smaller and farther away than they really are
explanation: The manual states that everything appears smaller in a convex mirror than it would look directly, and things also seem farther away than they really are.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.4.2 Seeing to the Sides and Rear, How to Use Mirrors

question: Which of the following is one of the manual's rules for using turn signals?
choice_a: Cancel the signal before completing the turn to avoid confusing others
choice_b: Signal early, well before you turn, to keep others from trying to pass you
choice_c: Signal only after beginning the turn
choice_d: Only signal if another vehicle is visible nearby
explanation: The manual's rule is to signal early, well before you turn, which is the best way to keep others from trying to pass you.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions, Turns

question: According to the manual, when should a turn signal be used before changing lanes?
choice_a: After the lane change is complete
choice_b: Only while the lane change is in progress
choice_c: Before changing lanes, so a driver you didn't see has a chance to react
choice_d: Turn signals are optional for lane changes
explanation: The manual says to put your turn signal on before changing lanes and change lanes slowly and smoothly, giving a driver you didn't see a chance to react.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions, Lane Changes

question: How can a driver warn following traffic of the need to slow down?
choice_a: Speed up first, then brake hard
choice_b: Turn off all lights so following drivers stay alert
choice_c: Give a few light taps on the brake pedal to flash the brake lights
choice_d: Roll down the window and wave
explanation: The manual states a few light taps on the brake pedal, enough to flash the brake lights, should warn following drivers.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions, Slowing Down

question: When is it appropriate to use four-way emergency flashers while a vehicle is moving, if legal in that state?
choice_a: While making a routine lane change
choice_b: While driving at highway speed in normal traffic
choice_d: While driving very slowly
explanation: The manual states drivers should alert following drivers by turning on emergency flashers if it is legal when they must drive slowly.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions, Driving Slowly

question: What does the manual say about a driver signaling other motorists that it is safe to pass?
choice_a: It is required at all uncontrolled intersections
choice_b: Drivers should not do this because it could cause a crash and lead to liability
choice_c: Only bus drivers are permitted to do this
choice_d: It is encouraged as a courtesy to other drivers
explanation: The manual warns that drivers should not signal others when it's safe to pass, because they could cause an accident and be blamed, costing thousands of dollars.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.1 Signal Your Intentions, Don't Direct Traffic

question: When about to pass a vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist, what should a driver assume and do?
choice_a: Assume they see you and that no signal is needed
choice_b: Use only the horn and never the headlights
choice_c: Always come to a complete stop before passing
choice_d: Assume they don't see you, and tap the horn lightly or flash lights from low to high beam and back
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to assume a vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist doesn't see them, and to tap the horn lightly or, at night, flash lights from low to high beam and back.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence, When Passing

topic: Making Yourself Visible in Low Light
question: At dawn, dusk, in rain, or snow, what does the manual recommend to make your vehicle easier to see?
choice_a: Rely on daytime running lights alone
choice_b: Turn on your headlights, using low beams
choice_c: Use only identification and clearance lights
choice_d: Turn on only the high beams at all times
explanation: The manual advises turning on headlights (not just identification or clearance lights) using low beams, since high beams can bother people even in the daytime.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence, When It's Hard to See

question: If you must stop on a road or shoulder, within what time period must you put out your emergency warning devices?
choice_b: 30 minutes
choice_d: 10 minutes
explanation: The manual states that if you must stop on a road or shoulder, you must put out your emergency warning devices within ten minutes.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence, When Parked at the Side of the Road

topic: Warning Device Placement on Divided Highways
question: If stopped on a one-way or divided highway, at what distances toward approaching traffic should warning triangles be placed?
choice_b: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet
choice_d: 50 feet, 100 feet, and 150 feet
explanation: The manual states that on a one-way or divided highway, warning devices should be placed 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward the approaching traffic.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence, Figure 2.8

topic: Warning Device Placement on Two-Lane Roads
question: If stopped on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, where should warning devices be placed?
choice_a: Warning devices are not required on two-lane roads
choice_b: Only 10 feet behind the vehicle
choice_d: Within 10 feet of the front or rear corners, and 100 feet behind and ahead of the vehicle
explanation: The manual states that on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, place warning devices within 10 feet of the front or rear corners to mark the vehicle, and 100 feet behind and ahead of it.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence, Figure 2.9

topic: Warning Devices Near a Hill or Curve
question: If a hill or curve blocks other drivers' view of a stopped vehicle, what should be done with the rearmost warning triangle?
choice_b: It should be left in its standard position regardless of sight distance
choice_c: It should be moved back down the road so warning is provided within the required sight distance
choice_d: It should be placed directly under the vehicle
explanation: The manual states that if line of sight is obstructed by a hill or curve, move the rear-most triangle back down the road so warning is provided within 500 feet.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 2, Driving Safely, 2.5.2 Communicating Your Presence, Figure 2.10
